issues.problem: The payoff loses its premise. The push-in starts at then-0.5 (about 39.2 s), and by 42.0 s the retina is cropped off the left edge (only a sliver remains), with its header faded out. So when the needle swings to HORIZONTAL and the lantern flares on 'right' (42.67 s), the viewer cannot see the horizontal bar (p5, landed on 'suddenly') that the machine got right. The only clue is the small caption.
issues.fix: Retarget the K2 push so the retina, the dial rack and the response meter and lantern all stay in frame at 'right' (frame centre between retina and meter, zoom of 1.25 or less). Or hold the camera wide until right+0.3 and push only through the 1.6 s tail. Keep hRet visible until after 'right'.

issues.problem: The silhouette craft falls short of the reference frame. The lab props (retina stand, patch board, racks, console) are flat vector rectangles with the same thin light outline on every edge, a grid of identical rounded rects, and no hand-cut irregularity or ornament. Depth is mostly two planes (window wall and machine row). Only a faint desk lamp (s01) and a blurred cable coil (s02) sit in the foreground, while the reference layers foreground furniture, mid-plane figures and a back wall through haze. The result reads as clean vector illustration more than paper-cut theatre.
issues.fix: In sets/lab.ts and ch01-s02-machine.ts: put rim light only on the window-facing edges instead of outlining everything, and add cut-paper detail (vent louvres, cable bundles over the rack tops, feet and casters, irregular panel edges). Add a dark foreground plane with parallax (desk and chair, coiled cables, a stool) and a haze layer between the windows and the machine, so the dolly and truck show three or more planes moving at different speeds.

issues.problem: The Rosenblatt puppet is generic, and its acting reads wrong. It enters cut by the right frame edge at about 17.5 s. From 18 to 21.5 s it stands hunched, head bowed, with a limp palm-out hand ('psychologist who built it' is spoken over a figure that looks dejected or bowing). Only at about 22.5 s does it straighten and present. The thin profile with white outline strokes lacks period or costume detail compared with the reference figures.
issues.fix: Stage an upright figure standing beside the console (or walking in from behind the racks rather than from the frame edge) before 'psychologist' (19.4 s). Keep the head level and looking at the machine, and turn and extend the arm on 'Frank Rosenblatt' (21.5 to 22.0 s). Give the puppet a more specific cut-paper silhouette (tie, rolled cuffs, clipboard or pencil; not a likeness) and drop the full-body outline stroke in favour of a rim on the window side.

issues.problem: The opening type does not stay up long enough. The title is fully legible from about 1.8 to 4.0 s, then fades just as the place stamp finishes typing (about 4.0 s). The stamp (48 characters) is fully readable for only about 1.2 s (4.0 to 5.2 s), and the shot then holds an empty plate before crossfading into a near-identical s02 frame. The spec asked for small caps; the title is set in upper and lower case.
issues.fix: Type the place stamp faster (complete by about 3.2 s) and hold both until about 5.4 s, then fade under the crossfade. Set the title in small caps as the script describes.

issues.problem: The visual count of mistakes does not match the spoken one. The narration has three wrongs and then 'right' ('wrong' / 'Wrong' / 'wrong again' / 'right'), but the screen shows four wrong presentations. p4 snaps to a wrong answer and is captioned on 'and then, quite', just as the voice turns toward 'suddenly, right', which blurs the turn.
issues.fix: Play p4 as a quick, uncaptioned, dimmed flick (no verdict caption or emphasis) so the readable rhythm is wrong, wrong, wrong, RIGHT. Or hold p3 through 'then' and let p4 lead directly into the correct p5 on 'suddenly'.

issues.problem: Shape crossfades on the retina overlap, so for a moment the outgoing horizontal bar and the incoming vertical bar make a '+' (visible at about 39.0 s). s02 shows a deliberate '+' at 'twenty by twenty', so a viewer may read it as a third class.
issues.fix: Clear the retina (fade out over about 0.15 s) before the next bar fades in, so the two never overlap.

issues.problem: The verdict captions ('presentation n · said "x" — wrong') are small italics (about 22 px at 1080p), amber on amber, and fade in slowly. At 29.5 s the caption is barely visible while 'wrong' is spoken at 30.16 s. A flies lantern also sits over the 'O' of 'RETINA · 20 × 20 PHOTOCELLS' at about 36.8 s.
issues.fix: Raise the caption to about 30 px with higher contrast (cream on a dark band) and a 0.2 s fade landing on the word. Move the top-left flies lantern clear of the retina header, or move the header down.

issues.problem: The Frank Rosenblatt name card sits at the lower left over the patch board, about 1,300 px from the figure on the right edge. The eye has to cross the whole frame to connect the name to the man.
issues.fix: Anchor the name card next to the figure (left of or below him, around x 1450 to 1700 at 1080p) on his plane, so it tracks the camera with him.

issues.problem: The 'dials' beat glows the rack dials at about 17.5 s (on 'motors could turn'), not on 'dials' (16.4 s). Between 16.0 and 17.0 s the racks sit unaccented while the word is spoken.
issues.fix: Add a soft highlight sweep across the dial racks on 'dials' (16.4 s), then keep the existing turning glints on 'motors could turn'.

issues.problem: The film has no fade-out. The last frame (44.75 s) is the full-brightness lantern close-up (mean luma about 71/255, the same as 43.5 s), so the film hard-cuts to black as the cue resolves. Separately, ffprobe reports 'Referenced QT chapter track not found' and render-report.final.chapters is null.
issues.fix: Add a fade to black over the last 0.8 to 1.0 s (or extend the tail by 1 s and fade). Fix the chapter mux in film-assemble so the chapter track is written.

best_moments: ch01-s02 at about 9.1 s: the '400 light cells' callout lands on 'light cells'; at about 12 s the '20' dimension rules on both axes land on 'twenty by twenty'. Exact, legible, motivated by the camera push.

ch01-s02 to ch01-s03 at 25.6 s: the iris closes on the console's meters and opens on the theatre's big response meter. It is a match on the meter and a strong change of world from labGreen to candleAmber.
ch01-s03 at about 32.0 s: on 'nudge', the fired dials turn with arc arrows and glints, and their threads thicken. The perceptron rule is visibly enacted, with needle snaps landing on each 'wrong'.
ch01-s03 at 42.67 s: the needle swings to HORIZONTAL and the paper lantern flares exactly on 'right', with a held, glowing tail.
ch01-s01 and ch01-s02: the venetian-blind light stripes on the floor and the backlit sash windows give the lab a real film-noir light source and a consistent mood.
